nodes.name: Hourly Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — every 12 h. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Reads every row from 'Payload Tracker' — the read side of the store, e.g. for a digest or a downstream sync. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Fetch Changes Since Watermark
nodes.notes: GET https://api.example.com/v1/payloads — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Normalize Records
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Normalize incoming payload records to a stable schema Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per payload (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Upsert into Airtable
nodes.notes: Upserts into Airtable's 'Payloads' table, matched on itemId — safe to re-run without creating duplicates. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Advance Watermark
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Advance the incremental watermark to the newest record seen Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Persist Watermark (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Payload Tracker', matched on itemId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Row Counts Match?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.processed >= 0 }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

parameters.text: =⚠️ ETL drift detected: {{ $json.processed }} rows vs expected

nodes.name: Raise Drift Alarm
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Gmail — subject is the first line of the message body, recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Enrich with Reference Data
nodes.notes: GET https://enrichment.example.com/v2/lookup — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Fold In Enrichment Fields
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes enrichedAt, enrichmentSource. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot 2
nodes.notes: Searches Airtable's 'Payloads' table by formula (={LastModified} > DATEADD(NOW(), -1, 'days')) for records the pipeline hasn't handled yet. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Compute Drift vs Snapshot
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Compare current metrics with the previous snapshot Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Payload Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

# Streamline a routine task for data transforms

**Pattern:** Workflow Automation · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers data-transforms work end to end across Google Sheets, Gmail and Airtable.

It moves through 20 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Load Previous Snapshot
3. Fetch Changes Since Watermark
4. Normalize Records
5. Fingerprint for Idempotency
6. Drop Already-Processed Items
7. Upsert into Airtable
8. Advance Watermark
9. Persist Watermark (Google Sheets)
10. Row Counts Match?
11. Raise Drift Alarm
12. Stamp Completion Time
13. Persist Run Metadata
14. Enrich with Reference Data
15. Fold In Enrichment Fields
16. Load Previous Snapshot 2
17. Compute Drift vs Snapshot
18. Summarize Run Stats
19. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
20. Send Summary to Gmail

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing data-transforms work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Load Previous Snapshot → Fetch Changes Since Watermark → Normalize Records → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Upsert into Airtable → Advance Watermark → Persist Watermark (Google Sheets) → Row Counts Match? → Raise Drift Alarm → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Load Previous Snapshot 2 → Compute Drift vs Snapshot → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Gmail → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Gmail → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Gmail aligned by hand for data transforms
- Data transforms work where "Fetch Changes Since Watermark" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Data transforms work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Gmail in step for data transforms, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Gmail are skipped, across all 23 nodes of this data-transforms build
- A failed Google Sheets or Gmail call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 23 nodes in this data-transforms build
- Every data-transforms run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets
- Fans the same result out to Airtable in the same run, for data transforms

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Airtable PAT; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The pipeline is incremental, not full-refresh: it stores a watermark (the last-seen timestamp) and only asks the source for records newer than that, which is what keeps a scheduled re-run cheap instead of re-pulling the entire dataset every time. The tradeoff is that a failed watermark write must be safe to retry — which is exactly why the destination write is an upsert, not a plain insert.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Manually roll the watermark back and re-run — confirm the upsert makes the replay safe (no duplicates).
2. Trigger a reconcile mismatch on purpose and confirm the drift alarm fires.
3. Point the source at a different platform and see how little else in the workflow has to change.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your data transforms process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole data-transforms payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
